# About this script
This script represents the primary data processing workflow for evaluating Mean Pairwise Distance (MPD) using raw functional traits. The pipeline executes the following steps:

1) Computes multi-trait Gower distances using raw trait data of terrestrial ferns from the Southern Atlantic Forest (SAF).

2) Calculates Standardized Effect Size of Mean Pairwise Distance (SES.MPD) under both abundance-weighted and presence/absence frameworks.

3) Fits linear models to evaluate relationships between SES.MPD and environmental drivers.

4) Tests model residuals for spatial structure using Moran's I and Spatial Eigenvector Maps (MEM).

5) Evaluates model robustness against sampling effort using Cook's distance correlations.

The results of this script will be part of Table 1, Appendix S11 and Appendix S12.

# Packages

Multiple packages are required to run this script, most of
them are available on CRAN, see below.

```{r}
# Clear workspace and free memory
gc()
rm(list = ls())

# Data Wrangling & Utilities
library(readxl)
library(openxlsx)
library(reshape2)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

# Functional Diversity & Distance Calculations
library(gawdis)
library(SYNCSA)
library(picante)

# Model Fitting, Selection & Diagnostics
library(bbmle)
library(car)
library(broom)
library(interactions)
library(jtools)

# Spatial Analysis
library(adespatial)
library(spdep)
library(sp)
library(SoDA)
library(nlme)

# Reproducibility settings
set.seed(811)
options(scipen = 999)
```

# Community Matrix 
Import site-by-species abundance data from the primary dataset and reshape into a matrix format filled with absolute taxon frequencies.

```{r}
# Load 'w_matrix' sheet containing abundance data
d <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "w_matrix")

# Reshape from long to wide format (sites x taxa)
w_matrix <- dcast(
  site ~ taxa,
  data = d,
  value.var = "FA_New",
  fun.aggregate = sum
) %>%
  column_to_rownames("site") %>%
  round(digits = 2)

# Inspect matrix dimensions and preview structure
head(w_matrix, 5L)
```

# Trait Matrix 
Now we load the trait matrix, that lives on t_matrix sheet. Then, we standardize and rework this data to transform on numerical, categorical and binary data.

```{r}
# Load 't_matrix' sheet from Excel
t <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = "t_matrix")

# View a specific subset of the trait data (example filter)
t[grepl(t$taxa, pattern = 'Macrothe'), ]$laminae_dissection

str(t)  # Check structure of trait data

# Convert categorical and numerical traits appropriately
t_matrix <- t %>%
  mutate(
    rhizome_type = as.factor(rhizome_type),
    laminae_dissection = as.numeric(laminae_dissection),
    frond_morphology = as.factor(frond_morphology)
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames('taxa')  # Set taxa as row names

glimpse(t_matrix)  # Overview of final structure
head(t_matrix)

# Check consistency between community and trait matrices
ncol(w_matrix)  # Number of taxa in community matrix
nrow(t_matrix)  # Number of taxa in trait matrix
```

# X Variables

Finally, we can load the predictor variables. Here we like to emphasize that soil data was obtained from SoilGrids v. 2.0 and from WorldClim v. 2.1. 

```{r}
# Load 'e_matrix' with environmental data
x_ncor <- read_xlsx(here("data/data_ferns.xlsx"), sheet = 'e_matrix') %>%
  filter(Site %in% rownames(w_matrix)) %>%  # Match only sites in w_matrix
  column_to_rownames('Site') %>%  # Use site names as row names
  mutate(Site = NULL, ref = NULL)  # Drop unused columns

head(x_ncor)  # Preview environmental variables
```

# Organize data 

We will use SYNCSA to organize our data in a list, matching taxa names and sites in all matrices.

```{r}
# Create a standardized data list using SYNCSA
org_data <- organize.syncsa(w_matrix, traits = t_matrix, envir = x_ncor)

# org_data  # Show the organized data list

# Check if trait and community taxa names match
identical(rownames(org_data$traits), colnames(org_data$community))

# glimpse(org_data$traits)  # Inspect the trait matrix in the list
```

# Functional Distance Matrix
Now we calculate the functional diversity to our data, we use here 3 groups, based on the type of trait (i.e., 1-competition, 2-protection and 3-reproduction). This method reduces discrepancies in the correlation of individual-trait and multi-trait matrices [(de Bello et al. 2021)](www.doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13537).
 

```{r}
# Compute functional distances with trait grouping 
full_trait <- gawdis(org_data$traits, groups = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3))
full_trait <- as.matrix(full_trait)  # Convert to matrix
```

# SES Mean Pairwise Distance (Abundance-Weighted)

Calculate Standardized Effect Size of MPD incorporating species abundances under a richness null model.

After, we will select the best model for each trait, as following:
1) Creating a list of models names (see Appendix S1 for the hypothesis of each model);
2) Elaborating the linear models, based on the list;
3) Select the most parsimonious models based on AICc;
4) Filter only the best model (dAICc = 0);
5) Save in a new object for summarize in a table.

```{r}
# Calculate Standardized Effect Size of MPD with abundance
ses_mpd_full <- picante::ses.mpd(
  org_data$community,
  full_trait,
  abundance.weighted = TRUE,
  null.model = "richness"
) |>
  rownames_to_column(var = 'Site')

# Merge MPD results with environmental data
ses <- cbind.data.frame(ses_mpd_full, org_data$environmental)

# Identify sites with significant deviation in functional diversity
ses_mpd_full %>% filter(mpd.obs.p < 0.1)  # More clustered
ses_mpd_full %>% filter(mpd.obs.p > 0.95)  # More overdispersed
```

# SES Mean Pairwise Distance (Presence/Absence)

Calculate non-weighted (presence/absence) SES MPD to evaluate functional structure independent of abundance.

```{r}
# Calculate SES MPD without abundance (presence/absence only)
ses_mpd_pa <- picante::ses.mpd(
  org_data$community,
  full_trait,
  abundance.weighted = FALSE,
  null.model = "richness"
) |>
  rownames_to_column(var = 'Site')

# Combine with environmental data
ses_pa <- cbind.data.frame(ses_mpd_pa, org_data$environmental)

# Check extreme SES values
ses_mpd_pa %>% filter(mpd.obs.p < 0.1)
ses_mpd_pa %>% filter(mpd.obs.p > 0.95)
```

# Candidate Model Formulation
Define formulas for the set of candidate hypotheses explaining functional diversity variation.

```{r}
models <- c(
  "ses_mpd_full ~ nitrogen",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ cec",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ clay",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ prec_seas",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ 1",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ prec_seas+ann_prec",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ cec+nitrogen",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec+max_temp_wam",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ ann_prec * prec_seas",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ nitrogen * clay",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam * prec_seas",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam + prec_warm",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ max_temp_wam * prec_warm",
  "ses_mpd_full ~ prec_warm"
)
```

# Evaluating models with abundance
Fit linear models adjusting for sampling effort (plot_size and samp_size) and perform model selection using AICc.

```{r}
m1 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m2 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ cec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m3 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ clay + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m4 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m5 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m6 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m7 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ 1 + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m8 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ prec_seas + ann_prec + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m9 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ cec + nitrogen + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m10 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec + max_temp_wam + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m11 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ ann_prec * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m12 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ nitrogen * clay + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)

m13 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam * prec_seas + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m14 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam + prec_warm + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m15 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ max_temp_wam * prec_warm + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)
m16 <- lm(
  mpd.obs.z ~ prec_warm + plot_size + samp_size,
  data = ses
)

# Perform model selection via AICc
sel_md <- AICctab(
  m1,
  m2,
  m3,
  m4,
  m5,
  m6,
  m7,
  m8,
  m9,
  m10,
  m11,
  m12,
  m13,
  m14,
  m15,
  m16,
  mnames = models,
  base = T,
  delta = T
)

# Extract best-supported model
sel_md %>%
  `class<-`("data.frame") %>%
  dplyr::filter(dAICc == 0)

sel_md_ab <- sel_md  # Save model selection
summary(m13)  # Summarize best model
model_ab <- m13  # Save final selected model

```

# Spatial Weight Matrix Construction

```{r}
# Project latitude/longitude to metric coordinates (UTM equivalent in km)
df_xy <- SoDA::geoXY(
  latitude = x_ncor$Lat,
  longitude = x_ncor$Long,
  unit = 1000
)

# Calculate Euclidean spatial distance and connectivity graph
dist <- dist(df_xy)
nb <- chooseCN(coordinates(df_xy), type = 4, plot.nb = FALSE)
distnb <- nbdists(nb, df_xy)

# Weight neighbors by distance (inverse)
fdist <- lapply(distnb, function(x) 1 - x / max(dist(df_xy)))

# Construct spatial list weights object
lw <- nb2listw(nb, style = 'B', glist = fdist, zero.policy = TRUE)
```

# Residual Diagnostics: Abundance Model

Inspect model residuals for spatial structure and perform Moran's I test via spatial eigenvector selection.

```{r}
# Get residuals
res <- residuals(model_ab)

# Perform Moran's I test for spatial autocorrelation
mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = TRUE)

# Store spatial autocorrelation summary
sac_ab <- data.frame(
  I = mem$global.test$obs,
  Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
) %>%
  mutate(model = as.character(model_ab$call)[2], .before = I) %>%
  `rownames<-`(NULL)
```

# Residual Diagnostics: Presence/Absence Model  

Inspect presence/absence model residuals for spatial structure.

```{r}
# Get residuals
res <- residuals(model_pa)

# Perform Moran's I test for spatial autocorrelation
mem <- mem.select(res, lw, method = "MIR", nperm = 999, p.adjust = T)

# Store spatial autocorrelation summary
sac_pa <- data.frame(
  I = mem$global.test$obs,
  Pvalue = mem$global.test$pvalue
) %>%
  mutate(model = as.character(model_pa$call)[2], .before = I) %>%
  `rownames<-`(NULL)
```

# Export Processed Data and Results (Appendix S11; Table 1)

Save model objects, data lists, model selection tables, and regression summaries to output directory.

We will use the results produced here as the Appendix S11 and in Table 1.

```{r}
#Raw data
saveRDS(model_ab, file = here("outputs/raw_ses_mod_ab.RDS"))
saveRDS(model_pa, file =here( "outputs/raw_ses_mod_pa.RDS"))
saveRDS(org_data, file = here("outputs/raw_ses_mod_data.RDS"))
saveRDS(ses, file = here("outputs/ses_mpd_full.RDS"))
saveRDS(ses_pa, file = here("outputs/ses_mpd_pa_full.RDS"))

# Spatial result
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  x = list(Moran = sac_pa, AIC = sel_md_pa),
  here(
  'outputs/ses_selection_binary.xlsx')
)
openxlsx::write.xlsx(
  x = list(Moran = sac_ab, AIC = sel_md_ab),
  here(
  'outputs/ses_selection_abundance.xlsx'
))

# Export models and coefficients
export_summs(
  model_ab,
  model_pa,
  digits = 3,
  model.names = c("SES with frequency", "SES binary"),
  statistics = c(
    R2 = "r.squared",
    "AIC",
    "df",
    'F-statistic' = 'statistic',
    N = 'nobs'
  ),
  error_format = "({statistic}, p = {p.value})",
  to.file = "xlsx",
  file.name = here( "outputs/ses.mpd.xlsx")
)
```

# Model Robustness and Cook's Distance Diagnostics

To demonstrate model robustness, here we will calculate Cook’s distance of models coefficients, which provides a global measure of the change in estimated parameters after removing a specific unit (e.g., a site) in linear models via a leave-one-out procedure (Snijders & Berkhof, 2008). It quantifies the influence of each observation on the overall model estimates.

After, we extract the resulting vector of Cook’s distance for all 28 evaluated sites of the i-th model we will correlate it with sample effort using Kendall rank correlation coefficient (τ). This non-parametric approach was selected because the sampling effort data did not follow a Gaussian distribution (Shapiro-Wilk test: P \< 0.05). The results of such analysis can indicate if there is a systematic error in the model's prediction, where sample effort is systematically associated with the influence of sites in prediction (τ \> 0.5; P-value \< 0.05) or there is no clear association. We also plotted the results to show visually the degree of influence of sites in prediction (Cj) and its sample effort, enabling the identification of influence patterns across poorly or well-sampled sites. For the phylogenetic corrected models we used the Cook’s distance average for the j-th site as Cj measurement.

```{r}
# Calculate Cook's distance values
ses$cook <- cooks.distance(model_ab)
ses_pa$cook <- cooks.distance(model_pa)

# Test correlation between Cook's distance and plot sample size
CS_ab <- cor.test(ses$cook, ses$samp_size, method = "kendall") %>% tidy() %>%
        mutate(model = "Abundance", .before = 1)

CS_pa <- cor.test(ses_pa$cook, ses_pa$samp_size, method = "kendall") %>% tidy() %>%
        mutate(model = "Presence", .before = 1)

CS_sum <- rbind(CS_ab, CS_pa)

write.xlsx(CS_sum, file = here("outputs/CS_cor_RSES.xlsx"))

# Plot diagnostic figures
tiff(filename = here("figs/cook_ses.tiff"), width = 180, height = 100, units = "mm", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1,2),  mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

# Panel 1: Abundance Model
plot(y = ses$cook, x= log10(ses$samp_size),
     cex.main = 0.8,
     cex.lab = .7,
     cex.sub = .6,
     cex.axis = .6,
     pch = 16,
     col=rgb(0,0,0,0.5),
     sub = "Kendall: 0.23; P = 0.09",
     main = "SES.MPD Abundance Weighted (Raw)",
     ylab = "Coefs. Cook's distance",
     xlab = "Sample size (m² - log10)",
        ylim = c(0,2))
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "red")

# Panel 2: Presence/Absence Model
plot(y = ses_pa$cook, x= log10(ses_pa$samp_size),
     cex.main = 0.8,
     cex.lab = .7,
     cex.sub = .6,
     cex.axis = .6,
     pch = 16,
     col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.5),
     sub = "Kendall: 0.01; P = 0.92",
     main = "SES.MPD Presence/Absence (Raw)",
     ylab = "Coefs. Cook's distance",
     xlab = "Sample size (m² - log10)", ylim = c(0, 2))
abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "red")
dev.off()

```
